title: First-person breath and smoke live in centimetres
note: Breath and smoke in front of the lens are centimetre-sized, low-opacity sprites; a world-sized one is an enormous white blob.
intent: Anything spawned in front of a first-person camera is centimetres from the lens, so a sprite sized for the world fills the screen as one enormous white blob. Spawn a puff 0.4–0.6 units ahead of the camera as 5–15 sprites of 0.02–0.08 world units, opacity ≤ 0.35, each shrinking as it fades over 2–3 s while drifting up and away; never one big sprite that grows. Verify from the default first-person camera during the effect: if the puff covers more than ~10% of the frame it is a blob, not breath. Rituals are player-triggered and visible both ways — the cigarette raises on the key press (never auto-lit at boot), the ember brightens per drag, the seated camera shows a composed view of the facing block’s lit windows.

check.note: First-person breath/smoke sprites are 0.02-0.08 world units and opacity <= 0.35 (an emitter must be tagged); a world-sized sprite in front of the lens is one enormous white blob.

port: In the rituals/first-person module, add breathEmitter to the scene, call spawnBreath(camera) from the ritual key handler sampled in update() from ctx.keys, and tickBreath(dt) every step; give the demo that triggers the ritual a name so the puff-coverage pixel check can run from the default first-person camera while the puff is alive.

evidence.note: 0.4–0.6 units ahead, sprites 0.02–0.08, 5–15 per puff, opacity ≤0.35, shrink over 2–3 s; >10% of frame is a blob
first-person controller is a mode toggle, not the default camera; debugCamera must override it and re-render synchronously
